dedupe_keys.name: nasa mav open source framework for modelling humans automation and their interactions in air traffic management and airspace design concepts

description: MAV (modeling, analysis and visualisation of air traffic management concepts) is a NASA Ames framework released as open source through the NASA Software Catalog (case ARC-17874-1, version 1.0 of June 2015). Contents: a modelling and analysis framework that represents humans, automation, and the interactions among humans and between humans and automation in air traffic management and airspace design concepts, so that the safety contribution of human operators' decisions and actions can be characterised; the catalogue notes that existing fast-time simulation does not precisely characterise the human role in safety assurance and that choosing the right level of abstraction for human performance models is hard. Producer: NASA Ames. Coverage: generic. Format and access: open source code for macOS, Windows and Linux, linked from the catalogue. Licence: NASA open source release. Caveats: a research prototype from 2015, and models of operators and automation must be built by the user. Simulation uses: agent-based safety analysis of air traffic procedures, evaluating automation concepts, and human factors in disruption and emergency scenarios for aviation. Related records: NASA TRAC (model-nasa-trac-trajectory-based-route-analysis-control) supports airspace design and traffic simulation.
